content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any secrets management task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple secrets management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Validate secrets management outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. When secrets management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Before starting secrets management work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen secrets management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Prefer explicit, readable secrets management solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. Document any non-obvious secrets management decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. When secrets management decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. Measure before optimizing any secrets management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
10. Re-check edge cases relevant to secrets management (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
11. Prefer the simplest secrets management approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of secrets management correctness.
- Do not skip documenting secrets management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic secrets management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new secrets management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these secrets management guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
